newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Singapore warns Africa developing will be tough.
newsitem.headline: Singapore warns Africa developing will be tough.

text.p: The emerging markets of Africa will face a tough task in trying to mimic the rapid pace of development of East Asia's "tiger economies", Singapore prime minister Goh Chok Tong said on Thursday.

Goh, part of a delegation of businessmen and politicians from the tiny Asian state visiting Southern Africa, said the global economic outlook was more difficult now than during the 1970s and 1980s when East Asian began to expand.
"The external environment is now far more competitive and less generous than when East Asia began to develop," Goh said.
He added that developed countries were suffering high unemployment, slower growth and that the end of the Cold War meant they had less need for economic allies in the developing world.
Goh said developing countries and regions would therefore have to find their own way in an increasingly competitive world economy.
"Every country must find its own way...it must understand its own people, their cultural attributes, and devise solutions to suit its specific conditions," he said.
Goh warned that failure to develop effectively would bring a heavy cost to African nations.
"For Africa, failure to adapt to the new global situation will not just mean slow growth and high unemployment, but possible economic backsliding, poverty, conflict and clashes," he said.
Goh said Singapore, with a population of just three million and no natural resources, was limited in the aid it could give.
"But within our capabilities, we will help in a concrete and practical way, both bilaterally and in concert with other countries and institutions," he said.
On Wednesday Singapore business representatives said they were looking to enter joint venture partnerships with local firms.

"We are confident that there are new investment opportunities and will assess what is possible...the type of investments we are looking at are likely to be joint venture partnerships," delegation leader Chandra Das told a news briefing.
From South Africa where it is visiting for four days, the Singapore business delegation will move on to Zimbabwe, Namibia and Botswana for similar exploratory investment talks.
